name: Isometric exploded view (2.5D)

source.description: An inspected 3D explainer separates an object into labelled layers along one axis to show what it is made of.

technique: An object's layers slide apart along a vertical axis with leader-line labels, turning an opaque device into a readable stack; then collapse back together.
purpose: Explain composition of hardware, software stacks, materials or organisations.
visual_behaviour: Stacked plates separate with staggered ease-out, labels draw out on leader lines, then the stack closes.
mechanics: Per-layer translateY with stagger from the top; leader lines with stroke-draw; optional slight camera tilt.

decomposition.timing: Separation about 0.8-1.2 s, labels 0.3 s each.

failure_modes: Isometric projection drawn inconsistently between layers

implementation.approach: Draw each layer as an isometric parallelogram (SVG) with flat top and side shading; translateY stagger; Studio.draw.connect for leader lines. Candidate composition once a brief needs it.

capability.approximation: Flat-shaded isometric SVG plates; loses lighting, depth of field and camera orbit.

provenance.observed: A chip is taken apart into stacked layers with labels (approx., from overview spacing).

licensing_notes: Technique only; never draw the reference's branded hardware.
